Print a bias and uncertainty corrected sample size result

Source: R/bucss-internal.R
print.bucss_power.Rd

Prints the aligned term/value table (the planned-study results followed by the rows echoing the planning inputs), then factual footer lines naming the design, the unit the sample size is counted in, and the largest assurance the prior result can support. Whole numbers print clean; other values print at getOption("bucss.digits", 3) significant figures. Only the display is rounded; the stored values keep full precision.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bucss_power'
print(x, digits = getOption("bucss.digits", 3L), ...)

Arguments

x

An object of class bucss_power.

digits

Significant figures for non-integer values; defaults to getOption("bucss.digits", 3).

...

Further arguments, ignored.

Value

x, invisibly.

Examples

result <- ss_buc_independent_t(t_observed = 3, n = c(50, 55),
  assurance = .90)
result
#>  term                  value
#>  necessary_n_per_group 1485 
#>  total_N               2970 
#>  actual_power          0.803
#>  ncp_adjusted          0.526
#>  t_observed            3    
#>  n_1                   50   
#>  n_2                   55   
#>  alpha_prior           0.05 
#>  alpha_planned         0.05 
#>  assurance             0.9  
#>  desired_power         0.8  
#> 
#> Design: Independent t test
#> Sample size unit: per group
#> Largest supportable assurance: .93

# Display only: the stored values keep full precision.
print(result, digits = 6)
#>  term                  value   
#>  necessary_n_per_group 1485    
#>  total_N               2970    
#>  actual_power          0.802709
#>  ncp_adjusted          0.526243
#>  t_observed            3       
#>  n_1                   50      
#>  n_2                   55      
#>  alpha_prior           0.05    
#>  alpha_planned         0.05    
#>  assurance             0.9     
#>  desired_power         0.8     
#> 
#> Design: Independent t test
#> Sample size unit: per group
#> Largest supportable assurance: .93
result$value[result$term == "ncp_adjusted"]
#> [1] 0.5262426
